name: MCP6567T-E_SN
title: 1.8 V low-power open-drain comparators, single, dual and quad
summary: A family of CMOS voltage comparators with rail-to-rail inputs, internal hysteresis and open-drain outputs, running from 1.8 V to 5.5 V on about 100 µA per comparator. High-to-low propagation delay is 56 ns typical at 1.8 V and 34 ns at 5.5 V. The output pull-up may go to a rail above or below VDD, up to 10.5 V absolute, for level shifting or wired-OR. MCP6567T-E/SN is the dual in an 8-pin SOIC on tape and reel, rated -40 °C to +125 °C.
key_figures: 100 µA typ per comparator (60 µA min, 130 µA max)
56 ns typ at VDD = 1.8 V; 34 ns typ at 5.5 V; 80 ns max
VSS – 0.3 V to VDD + 0.3 V at 5.5 V
open drain, pull-up 1.6 V to 5.5 V; 10.5 V absolute

curves.title: Figure 4-1. Internal hysteresis removes output chatter from input noise
curves.conditions: VDD = 5.0 V; time base 100 ms/div

circuits.title: Typical application circuit
circuits.description: Inverting comparator with external hysteresis. VIN drives the inverting input; R2 and R3 divide VDD to set the reference on the non-inverting input, and RF feeds the output back to that node to add hysteresis. The open-drain output is pulled up to a +3 V rail while the comparator runs from +5 V, so the output swings to a different level than the supply.

circuits.title: AC and DC test circuit
circuits.description: The circuit the AC and DC characteristics are measured in. Two 200 kΩ resistors hold the non-inverting input at VDD/2, the inverting input is driven by VIN = VSS, and the open-drain output is pulled up by 20 kΩ to VPU = VDD and loaded by 25 pF to ground.
notes: VSS = 0 V.

circuits.title: Figure 4-3. Protecting the analog inputs
circuits.description: Series resistors R1 and R2 limit the current that each input can draw when its source swings below VSS, and diodes D1 and D2 clamp each input to VDD so it cannot rise far above the supply; the resistors also limit the diode current. R3 is the feedback resistor to the output and R4 the output pull-up to VPU. Each series resistor should be at least (VSS minus the lowest expected input) divided by 2 mA.
notes: The diodes may sit on the source side of R1 and R2 instead; their current must then be limited some other way, and the resistors act as inrush limiters.

circuits.title: Figure 4-4. Non-inverting circuit with hysteresis, single supply
circuits.description: VIN reaches the non-inverting input through R1, and RF from the output back to that input sets the hysteresis. A fixed VREF sits on the inverting input. RPU pulls the open-drain output up to VPU. The trip points are given by the non-inverting hysteresis equations.

circuits.title: Figure 4-6. Inverting circuit with hysteresis
circuits.description: VIN drives the inverting input. R2 and R3 divide VDD for the non-inverting input and RF from the output to that node adds hysteresis; RPU pulls the output to VPU. For the trip points the divider is replaced by its Thevenin equivalent V23 behind R23.

circuits.title: Figure 4-8. Thevenin equivalent of the inverting circuit
circuits.description: The inverting hysteresis circuit with its R2–R3 divider replaced by a source V23 behind R23, which feeds the non-inverting input and meets RF from the output there.

circuits.title: Figure 4-11. Unused comparator
circuits.description: One spare section of an MCP6569 with its inverting input tied to VDD and its non-inverting input to ground: the output cannot toggle, so it causes no crosstalk, and the section draws minimal current. The output is left open.

circuits.title: Figure 4-12. Precise inverting comparator
circuits.description: An MCP6291 op amp amplifies the input ahead of the comparator to raise DC precision. VIN enters through R1 to the op amp's inverting input, R2 is its feedback resistor, and its non-inverting input sits at VREF. The op amp output drives the comparator's non-inverting input; the comparator's inverting input is at VREF. RPU pulls the comparator output up to VPU.

circuits.title: Figure 4-13. Windowed comparator
circuits.description: Both halves of an MCP6567 compare VIN with two thresholds: section A has VRT on its non-inverting input and VIN on its inverting input, section B has VIN on its non-inverting input and VRB on its inverting input. The two open-drain outputs share one pull-up, forming a wired AND, so VOUT is high only while VIN lies between VRB and VRT (VRT > VRB).

circuits.title: Figure 4-14. Bistable multivibrator
circuits.description: An oscillator. R1 from VREF and R2 from the output set the non-inverting input with positive feedback; R3 from the output charges C1 on the inverting input. VREF must lie between VSS (ground) and VDD for it to oscillate, and the output duty cycle moves with VREF. RPU pulls the output up to VPU.

equations.name: Input series resistor for protection
equations.expr: R1 ≥ (VSS – V1min) / 2 mA;  R2 ≥ (VSS – V2min) / 2 mA

where.V1min, V2min: lowest voltage expected at each input source

equations.name: Trip points, non-inverting circuit
equations.expr: VTLH = VREF·(1 + R1/RF) – VOL·(R1/RF);  VTHL = VREF·(1 + R1/RF) – VOH·(R1/RF)

where.VTLH: input voltage at which the output goes low to high
where.VTHL: input voltage at which the output goes high to low

equations.name: Trip points, inverting circuit
equations.expr: VTHL = VOH·R23/(R23 + RF) + V23·RF/(R23 + RF);  VTLH = VOL·R23/(R23 + RF) + V23·RF/(R23 + RF)

where.VTHL: input voltage at which the output goes high to low
where.VTLH: input voltage at which the output goes low to high
where.VOL, VOH: output low and high levels (Figures 2-21 and 2-24 give typical VOL)

operation.text: MCP6566 is a single comparator, with pin variants MCP6566R and MCP6566U; MCP6567 is a dual and MCP6569 a quad. All run from one supply of 1.8 V to 5.5 V, draw about 100 µA per comparator, and have open-drain outputs. A push-pull version of the family is the MCP6561/1R/1U/2/4.

Two input stages work in parallel, giving three regions: low, middle and high common-mode voltage. The common-mode range reaches 0.3 V beyond each rail while offset stays low across it; offset is tested at both VSS – 0.3 V and VDD + 0.3 V. The inputs are CMOS with very low bias current.

Built-in hysteresis of 1 mV to 5 mV keeps the output from chattering on the comparator's own input noise while leaving offset accuracy intact (Figure 4-1). VOS is the midpoint of the two trip points and VHYST the gap between them.

ESD diodes at the inputs clamp an input pulled a diode drop under VSS, or well over VDD. The external circuit must keep the input currents and voltages within the absolute maximum ratings: series resistors limit current drawn out of an input pin, and external diodes to VDD stop the input rising too high. With VCM under VSS the input pins can source a large current, so high-impedance sources may need a narrower usable range.
The output does not invert when an input goes beyond either supply rail (Figure 2-3).

The output needs a pull-up resistor. The pull-up voltage may be above or below VDD, which allows level shifting, and outputs can be wired together as a wired-OR. The output stage keeps shoot-through current small when it switches. Toggle frequency reaches about 4 MHz.

Resistors around the comparator give wider, chosen trip points. Hysteresis stops chatter when one input moves slowly past the other, keeps systems such as thermostats from cycling too often, and cuts the extra supply current that chatter draws. The non-inverting form uses two resistors (Figure 4-4), the inverting form three (Figure 4-6).

VDD sits 1.8 V to 5.5 V above VSS; the other pins normally stay between the two. In single-supply use VSS is ground. Put a 0.01 µF to 0.1 µF bypass capacitor within 2 mm of VDD for good edge rates; sharing a bulk capacitor with other analog parts up to 100 mm away is allowed but not needed.

Small loads such as logic inputs barely change propagation delay (Figure 2-32). Larger capacitance lowers the output slew rate and raises delay, and supply current climbs with toggle frequency, more so with heavier capacitive loads (Figure 2-20).

Board leakage can exceed the 1 pA typical bias current at 25 °C: about 10^12 Ω between nearby traces in low humidity passes 5 pA at 5 V. A guard ring around the sensitive input, held at that input's voltage, reduces it. Inverting use: the guard ring connects to VIN+ (the reference, such as VDD/2 or ground) and VIN- reaches its pad without touching the ring. Non-inverting use: VIN+ reaches its pad without touching the ring and the ring connects to VIN-.

Keep analog and digital traces apart: an output trace close to the inputs can couple its full swing back and make the comparator oscillate, so route output traces away from the input pins. On SC70 and SOT-23 the output (pin 1) is separated from +IN by the supply pin 2; on the dual and quad packages OUT and -IN are pins 1 and 2, next to each other, and need the recommended layout.
Tie a spare section's inverting input to VDD and its non-inverting input to VSS (Figure 4-11); the output then holds still, causes no crosstalk and the section draws minimal current.

A precision op amp ahead of the comparator raises DC accuracy (Figure 4-12). Two sections with wired outputs form a window comparator whose output is high only between two thresholds (Figure 4-13). With RC feedback the part becomes an oscillator whose duty cycle follows VREF (Figure 4-14).
A SPICE macro model for the MCP6566/7/9 covers voltage, current, resistance, temperature and noise behaviour; it is written for PSpice and is checked only inside the specified operating range.
